findings.body: The doc comment says "at most `limit` characters," but the `None` branch returns `head` (which is `limit` chars) plus `…` (1 char) = `limit + 1` chars. The tests confirm this by asserting `<= 21` for a limit of 20. If `limit` is set to a platform ceiling (e.g. GitHub's check-run title limit), the result can exceed it by one character, defeating the purpose of the function. The head should take `limit - 1` chars so the ellipsis fits within the limit.
findings.title: Reserve room for the ellipsis when shortening to a character limit

value.summary: The new `summarise` module provides text-shortening helpers for check-run and finding titles. The code is safe — character-based slicing avoids the multibyte panic the comments warn about, and `first_sentence`'s byte slicing is safe because `.` is ASCII. One minor issue: `shorten` can return `limit + 1` characters because the ellipsis is not counted toward the limit, contradicting the documented contract.
